spaces.name: Product price classes
spaces.description: Budget / standard / premium comparisons of equivalent products — helps pick the right class when building an offer

articles.title: How to use the price classes
articles.body:
## Which class to use, and when

An offer should default to **standard** class products. Deviating is only justified when the customer clearly signals a budget or premium requirement.

**Signals pointing to budget:**
- customer writes 'cheapest', 'value', 'budget', 'keep the price down'
- public/social project with tight funding
- large-quantity order where unit price dominates

**Signals pointing to standard (the default):**
- no explicit price or quality requirement
- a typical installation project with nothing unusual

**Signals pointing to premium:**
- customer writes 'premium', 'best', 'top quality', 'ABB', 'Schneider'
- hotel, hospital, or a flagship public building
- projects where the brand on the enclosure is visible to the end user
- a specific certification is required (e.g. EMC for industrial sites)

Each category below has a class table with concrete SKUs and selection guidance.

children.title: Photocell (dusk) sensors — price classes
children.body:
## Photocell sensors — class comparison

| Class | SKU | Brand | Mounting | Max current | IP | Net price | When to choose |
|-------|-----|-------|----------|-------------|-----|-----------|----------------|
| **Budget** | EM-012-10371 (Timeguard NE-71) | Timeguard (GB) | DIN | 6 A | IP65 (head) | £14.90 | Low price; DIN acceptable; EMC included |
| **Standard** | EM-012-10335 (Schneider AR-35) | Schneider (FR) | Surface | 6 A | IP65 | £26.50 | Most exterior projects; surface mount with no back box; the usual recommendation |
| **Premium** | EM-012-10277 (ABB TW-77) | ABB (CH) | DIN | **16 A** | IP44 | £27.20 | Large circuits > 6 A; ABB specification; car parks and yards |

**Important:**
- AR-35 (Standard) and the NE-71 remote head (Budget) are IP65 — suitable outdoors
- TW-77 (Premium) is only IP44 — the enclosure must provide the weather protection
- NE-71 with its remote head: the control unit can sit inside the consumer unit

**Common mistake:** Using AR-35 (6 A) to switch large LED floodlight arrays directly without checking the circuit current.

spaces.name: Installation requirements & standards
spaces.description: IP ratings, certifications and current limits — matching products to the installation environment

articles.title: IP ratings — what goes where
articles.body:
## Matching the IP rating to the environment

| Environment | Minimum IP | Reason |
|-------------|-----------|--------|
| Dry interiors (office, living room) | IP20 | No moisture risk |
| Garages, cellars, corridors | IP44 | Splashing, floor washing |
| Bathroom zone 2 (BS 7671) | IP44 | IET Wiring Regs requirement |
| Sheltered outdoor (canopy, porch) | IP44 | Wind-driven rain |
| Exposed outdoor | **IP65** | Jets of water |
| Prone to flooding | **IP67** | Temporary immersion |

**Practical consequences for the offer:**
- Photocell sensor outdoors → min IP65 → Schneider AR-35 (EM-012-10335) or Timeguard NE-71 head (EM-012-10371)
- Time switch in a sheltered outdoor spot → IP44 → BG BG-27 (EM-022-11527) or Timeguard TP-28 (EM-023-11928)
- Time switch on a kitchen terrace → IP54 → Finder FN-52 (EM-023-11752)
- Leak detector in a server room with sudden-flood risk → IP67 → ABB AS-12 (EM-015-11212)

**Note:** Installing a device with an insufficient IP rating can void the warranty and breach BS 7671.

articles.title: Certifications required for different project types
articles.body:
## Certifications — when each is required

### CE / UKCA — mandatory for all
All electrical products placed on the market must carry CE and/or UKCA marking. **Every product in our catalogue is CE/UKCA marked.**

### RoHS — restriction of hazardous substances
Mandatory for electrical equipment. **Almost all our products carry RoHS.** Exception: Schneider TH-40 (EM-014-10840, CE/UKCA only). Where RoHS is required (hospitals, schools, public buildings), do not offer the TH-40.

### EMC — electromagnetic compatibility
Not required for standard installations, but **required in:**
- factories and production sites
- hospitals and medical facilities
- public tenders (often stated explicitly in the spec)
- near sensitive equipment (server rooms, metering stations)

**Products with EMC certification in the range:**
| Category | SKU | Brand |
|----------|-----|-------|
| Photocell DIN | EM-012-10371 (Timeguard NE-71) | Timeguard |
| Photocell DIN 16A | EM-012-10277 (ABB TW-77) | ABB |
| Acoustic DIN | EM-013-10695 (Legrand LX-95) | Legrand |
| Thermostat DIN | EM-014-10842 (Finder FN-42) | Finder |
| Plug-in timer weekly | EM-022-11696 (Hager EZ-96) | Hager |
| Surface time switch IP44 | EM-023-11928 (Timeguard TP-28) | Timeguard |

**On public tenders:** Always check the specification for EMC requirements — select from the list above.

articles.title: Current rating — when you need an interposing relay
articles.body:
## Matching the product to the circuit load

| Current limit | Products | Notes |
|---------------|----------|-------|
| **6 A** (1380 W @ 230 V) | Most photocell and acoustic switches | Enough for 1–3 LED fittings |
| **10 A** (2300 W @ 230 V) | ABB SN-50, Finder FN-52 | Direct switching of medium circuits |
| **16 A** (3680 W @ 230 V) | ABB TW-77, all plug-in timers | Large lighting circuits |

### When to use an interposing relay
If the load exceeds 16 A, **always** add a relay or contactor. Signals:
- switching many exterior fittings (car parks, warehouses)
- switching motors (pumps, actuators)
- switching heaters and immersion loads > 3.5 kW

### Quick calculator
- total power ÷ 230 V = current in amps
- Example: 20 fittings × 50 W = 1000 W → 1000/230 = 4.35 A → within 6 A
- Example: 40 fittings × 50 W = 2000 W → 2000/230 = 8.7 A → needs a 10 A product or a relay

**When building the offer:** If the customer gives a fitting count or total wattage, always check the chosen sensor/timer can carry the load.

articles.title: Kits & compatibility — overview
articles.body:
## Recommended product kits

The articles below describe common product combinations for specific installation use cases. Each kit lists:
- required components
- selection by price class
- critical compatibility warnings
- common ordering mistakes

Use these kits as a checklist when building an offer — pay particular attention to the sections marked ⚠️.

children.title: Exterior lighting — complete control kit
children.body:
## Exterior lighting — complete kit

Full automation of exterior lighting needs two control devices:
1. **Photocell sensor** — switches lighting on automatically at dusk
2. **Time switch** — switches lighting off at a set night-time hour (e.g. 23:00), saving energy

Wired in series (photocell → time switch → lighting): on at dusk, off at the chosen hour.

### Recommended kits

**Budget kit (DIN):**
- Sensor: Timeguard NE-71 (EM-012-10371) — £14.90
- Time switch: Timeguard TP-28 (EM-023-11928) — £20.80

**Standard kit (surface):**
- Sensor: Schneider AR-35 (EM-012-10335) — £26.50
- Time switch: Timeguard TP-28 (EM-023-11928) — £20.80

**Premium kit (large circuits, commercial):**
- Sensor: ABB TW-77 (EM-012-10277) — £27.20 (16 A)
- Time switch: Finder FN-52 (EM-023-11752) — £30.20 (IP54)

### Selection notes
- **Current:** Check the total circuit draw. Above 6 A you need a 16 A sensor (ABB TW-77) or an interposing relay
- **IP:** Both devices must carry an IP rating appropriate to the mounting position
- **Series wiring:** The photocell and time switch can have different mounting types — that is fine

children.title: Underfloor heating — thermostat and required accessories
children.body:
## Underfloor heating — complete kit

⚠️ **CRITICAL ORDERING MISTAKE:** The Heatmiser HM-97 and Finder FN-42 thermostats require a **24 V AC/DC** supply. Wiring them directly to 230 V mains destroys the unit instantly.

### Kits by installation

**Standard — 24 V circuit (central manifold):**
- Thermostat: Heatmiser HM-97 (EM-014-10797) — £24.80
- **24 V transformer — required** (rating ≥ sum of actuator draw × 1.3)
- Thermal actuators (specify separately)

**Industrial / tender (EMC required):**
- Thermostat: Finder FN-42 (EM-014-10842) — £33.10
- **24 V transformer — required**

**Premium — direct 230 V (no transformer):**
- Thermostat: Schneider TH-40 (EM-014-10840) — £38.30
- No transformer — runs from 230 V mains
- Note: no RoHS — do not use where RoHS is required

### When 24 V, when 230 V
- **24 V (Heatmiser/Finder):** existing 24 V system, central manifold with many actuators, EMC requirements
- **230 V (Schneider):** new install, no 24 V available, hotel/apartment (visible enclosure)

**Leaving the transformer out of the offer is one of the most common mistakes when quoting 24 V thermostats.**

children.title: CCTV — IP camera and power
children.body:
## CCTV system — kit components

### Minimum components for a working system
1. **IP camera** (e.g. Hikvision VL-93, EM-042-12693)
2. **Power** — a PoE switch or a dedicated 12 V DC power supply
3. **NVR recorder** (e.g. Dahua DH-25, EM-045-13525) or a cloud option (optional on small installs)
4. **Cabling** Cat5e/Cat6 (up to 100 m for PoE)

### PoE vs dedicated power supply

**PoE (Power over Ethernet) — preferred:**
- one cable for signal and power
- easier to install and service
- needs a PoE switch or PoE injector

**Dedicated 12 V power supply:**
- when the camera has no PoE, or there is no PoE switch
- the supply voltage **must** match the camera spec (check the datasheet)
- MEAN WELL supplies are in the catalogue — size for the total load

### Common mistakes
- Ordering a camera with no power supply or PoE switch — the camera won't work
- Voltage mismatch on the supply — camera damage
- Undersized supply feeding several cameras — check total power draw

**When quoting cameras:** Always include a power supply or PoE switch — don't leave the customer with a camera and no power.

children.title: Video intercom — complete kit
children.body:
## Video intercom — kit components

### Minimum components
1. **Outdoor panel** (camera and call button)
2. **Indoor monitor** (screen and door release button)
3. **Power supply** — usually 12–18 V DC (check whether it is in the kit or separate)
4. **Electric strike or lock** — if the customer wants remote release

### Kits in the catalogue
- One-family: Aiphone JO-42 (EM-052-13942) — panel + monitor + PSU included
- Multi-tenant: Urmet UR-58 (EM-053-14358) — modular system for many flats

### Selection notes
- **Number of flats:** One-family kits = 1 monitor. Multiple flats → a multi-tenant system
- **Cable:** Check the documentation — usually 2-wire or Cat5/Cat6 depending on the system
- **Gate release:** If the customer wants remote release, make sure an electric strike is in the offer

**Common mistake:** Ordering only the monitor or only the panel — the system only works as a complete kit.

### Warranty procedure
1. Customer reports the fault in writing
2. We issue an RMA within 1 working day
3. Customer returns the faulty product (carriage refunded if the claim is upheld)
4. Fault assessment: up to 5 working days
5. Replacement or repair: up to 14 days after assessment

### Warranty does not cover
- mechanical damage, or water ingress on a product without a suitable IP rating
- damage caused by exceeding the rated current
- products with the label or serial number removed

**When selling Schneider and ABB:** the 3-year warranty is a selling point that justifies the higher price.

articles.title: Returns and complaints policy
articles.body:
## Returns and complaints

### Return without giving a reason
- Window: **14 days** from delivery
- Applies to: consumers (B2C) only, under the Consumer Contracts Regulations
- B2B customers: no statutory right of return — by contract only
- Product must be unused, in its original packaging

### Complaint under statutory rights
- Window: **up to 6 years** in England & Wales (Consumer Rights Act; B2C)
- The customer may request repair, replacement, a price reduction or a refund

### Goods not matching the order
- Report within **5 working days** of delivery
- Documentation: a photo showing the damage or the wrong product
- Review: up to 2 working days
- Correction: replacement or missing goods at no extra cost

### Products not eligible for return
- items specially ordered for a project (outside the catalogue)
- products with a broken seal or no packaging

articles.title: Pennine Manufacturing — factory lighting upgrade
articles.body:
## Pennine Manufacturing — factory exterior lighting upgrade

**Customer:** Pennine Manufacturing (industrial manufacturer)
**Scope:** Automating exterior lighting for the factory yard and car park
**Value:** ~£9,500 net

### Locations and requirements
- Works car park — 8 lighting columns
- Entrance and gate — 4 fittings
- Loading dock — 6× 200 W floodlights (1200 W total, ~5.2 A)

### Product selection
**Photocell DIN sensors with EMC (industrial site — EMC required in the spec):**
- 12× Timeguard NE-71 (EM-012-10371) — DIN, EMC, remote outdoor head
- Loading dock (circuit > 6 A): 3× ABB TW-77 (EM-012-10277) — 16 A, EMC

**Weekly time switches with EMC (night switch-off at 23:00):**
- 18× Timeguard TP-28 (EM-023-11928) — IP44, EMC, −20 °C

### Lessons for similar projects
1. Industrial sites **always** require EMC — check the catalogue before sending the offer
2. Car park and yard = outdoor mounting → min IP44 for the board, IP65 for the sensor head
3. Weekly (not daily) time switches — sunrise/sunset times shift across the seasons
4. The customer initially wanted cheaper non-EMC products — accepted once the requirements were explained
5. 15% discount granted (£5k–20k tier, Sales Lead approval)

articles.title: Meridian Developments — 6-storey office automation
articles.body:
## Meridian Developments — 6-storey office automation

**Customer:** Meridian Developments (commercial developer)
**Scope:** Stairwell lighting + underfloor heating
**Value:** ~£4,200 net

### Customer requirements
- Stairwell lighting: 'no visible back boxes, clean finish'
- Thermostats: 'energy efficient and EMC certified — we have a server room in the building'

### Product selection
**Acoustic switches (stairwells, flush, ABB brand on the enclosure):**
- 36× ABB SN-50 (EM-013-10750) — flush, max 30 s (short office corridors)

**Underfloor heating thermostats (DIN, EMC, 24 V):**
- 36× Finder FN-42 (EM-014-10842) — DIN, CE + UKCA + RoHS + EMC, 24 V
- 2× 24 V transformers (sized to the total actuator draw)

### Lessons
1. Premium customer (developer) → ABB/Finder despite the higher price — brand and certificates as the argument
2. **24 V transformers included in the offer** — the classic mistake is forgetting them
3. The customer asked about RoHS on the thermostats — Finder FN-42 complies (the Schneider TH-40 does not)
4. 10% discount (£2k–5k tier)
5. Order split into 3 tranches to match the construction schedule

articles.title: Harbourside Pharma — security system expansion
articles.body:
## Harbourside Pharma — security system expansion

**Customer:** Harbourside Pharma (pharmaceutical company, temperature-controlled warehouse)
**Scope:** CCTV + leak detectors in the server and chiller rooms
**Value:** ~£3,000 net

### Customer requirements
- RoHS and CE/UKCA documentation for every device
- Handover record with serial numbers
- Single invoicing source (everything through us)

### Product selection
**CCTV:**
- 8× Hikvision VL-93 IP cameras (EM-042-12693) — indoor
- 8-port PoE switch (ordered via partner, invoiced by us)
- Dahua DH-25 NVR (EM-045-13525)

**Leak detectors (under chillers and AC units):**
- 6× ABB AS-12 (EM-015-11212) — IP67, local audible alarm
- Rationale: server room = no Wi-Fi (Faraday cage), a local alarm is essential

### Lessons
1. Pharmaceutical environment → **always ask about documentation requirements before the offer**
2. Leak detectors: IP67 justified — flooding in chiller rooms can be sudden
3. The customer asked for the ESP Wi-Fi unit — switched to ABB after discussion (no Wi-Fi in the server room)
4. Single invoicing source = value — the customer avoids invoices from 3 suppliers
5. Net-30 for a new customer — accepted after references were provided
